## (2) Paccayaniddesa

Root condition: The six roots are a condition by way of root condition for the mental states associated with the roots and for the materiality produced by those roots (mind-produced materiality and rebirth kamma-produced materiality).

Object condition: The visible-data base is a condition by way of object condition for the eye-consciousness element and its associated mental states. The sound base...

(The sound base) is a condition by way of object condition for the ear-consciousness element and its associated mental states. The odour base is a condition by way of object condition for the nose-consciousness element and its associated mental states. The flavour base is a condition by way of object condition for the tongue-consciousness element and its associated mental states. The tangible-data base is a condition by way of object condition for the body-consciousness element and its associated mental states.

The visible-data base, sound base, odour base, flavour base, and tangible-data base are conditions by way of object condition for the mind element and its associated mental states. All phenomena are conditions by way of object condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated mental states.

Taking whatever phenomenon as an object, whichever mental states such as consciousness and mental factors arise, those phenomena are conditions by way of object condition for those mental states.

Predominance condition: Desire-predominance is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated mental states and for the materiality produced by that desire. Energy-predominance is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated mental states and for the materiality produced by that energy. Consciousness-predominance is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated mental states and for the materiality produced by that consciousness. Investigation-predominance is a condition by way of predominance condition for its associated mental states and for the materiality produced by that investigation.

Giving weight to whatever phenomenon, whichever mental states such as consciousness and mental factors arise, those phenomena are conditions by way of predominance condition for those mental states.

Proximity condition: The eye-consciousness element and its associated mental states are conditions by way of proximity condition for the mind element and its associated mental states. The mind element and its associated mental states are conditions by way of proximity condition for the mind-consciousness element and its associated mental states.

The ear-consciousness element and its associated mental states are conditions by way of proximity condition for the mind element and its associated mental states. Result condition: The four mental resultant aggregates are related to one another by result condition.

Based on those, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, displeasure arises. Having emerged from jhāna, one enjoys and relishes the jhāna. Based on that jhāna, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises. When the jhāna has disappeared, displeasure arises for one who feels regret.

(3) A wholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by object condition: an arahant, having emerged from the path, reviews the path. He reviews wholesome states formerly well-performed. ## Upanissaya-paccayo
Wholesome state is related to wholesome state by way of strong support condition: there are three kinds—object strong support, proximity strong support, and natural strong support.

Object strong support: having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the observance day duties, one reflects on that with esteem. One reflects on wholesome deeds previously well-performed with esteem. Having emerged from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna with esteem. Learners reflect on change-of-lineage with esteem. They reflect on purification with esteem. Learners, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path with esteem.

Adaptation is related to change-of-lineage... adaptation is related to purification... change-of-lineage is related to the path... purification is related to the path by way of strong support condition.

Natural strong support: depending on faith, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the observance day duties, induces jhāna, induces insight, induces the path, induces direct knowledge, induces attainment. Depending on virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the observance day duties, induces jhāna, induces insight, induces the path, induces direct knowledge, induces attainment. Faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom are related to faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom by way of strong support condition.

The Path is a condition for learners for the analytical insight of meaning (attha-paṭisambhidā), the analytical insight of the Dhamma (dhamma-paṭisambhidā), the analytical insight of language (nirutti-paṭisambhidā), the analytical insight of eloquence (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā), and for the knowledge of skill in what is possible and impossible (ṭhānāṭhāna-kosalla) by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Wholesome dhamma is a condition for unwholesome dhamma by way of decisive support condition: object-decisive support and natural decisive support.

Object-decisive support: Having given a gift, having undertaken virtue, having performed the duties of the observance day, one gives weight to that wholesome act and enjoys it, delights in it; giving weight to that wholesome act, lust arises, wrong view arises. Giving weight to wholesome acts well-performed in the past, one enjoys them, delights in them; giving weight to those acts, lust arises, wrong view arises. Having emerged from a jhāna, one gives weight to the jhāna and enjoys it, delights in it; giving weight to that jhāna, lust arises, wrong view arises.
147:
Natural decisive support: Depending on faith, one manifests conceit and holds wrong views. Depending on virtue, learning, generosity, or wisdom, one manifests conceit and holds wrong views. Faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom are conditions for lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and longing (patthanā) by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Wholesome dhamma is a condition for indeterminate dhamma by way of decisive support condition: object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support.

Object-decisive support: An Arahant, having emerged from the Path, gives weight to the Path and reviews it.

Proximity-decisive support: Wholesome is a condition for emergence; the Path is for Fruition; adaptation (anuloma) is for the fruition attainment of a learner; the wholesome of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception of one emerging from the attainment of cessation is a condition for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition.

Natural decisive support: Depending on faith, one torments oneself, exhausts oneself, and experiences suffering rooted in seeking. Depending on virtue, learning, generosity, or wisdom, one torments oneself, exhausts oneself, and experiences suffering rooted in seeking. Faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom are conditions for bodily pleasure (kāyika-sukha), bodily pain (kāyika-dukkha), and fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. Wholesome kamma is a condition for resultants (vipāka) by way of decisive support condition. An Arahant, depending on the Path, produces functional attainments not yet arisen, enters into attainments already arisen, and practices insight on formations as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. The Path is a condition for an Arahant for the analytical insight of meaning, the analytical insight of the Dhamma, the analytical insight of language, the analytical insight of eloquence, and for the knowledge of skill in what is possible and impossible by way of decisive support condition. ## Purejāta-paccaya

Indeterminate state is related to indeterminate state by pre-existence condition (purejāta-paccaya). There are two types: object pre-existence (ārammaṇa-purejāta) and base pre-existence (vatthu-purejāta).

Object pre-existence: An Arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self through insight. He contemplates the ear... nose... tongue... body... visible object... sound... smell... taste... touch... base-matter as impermanent, suffering, and non-self through insight; with the divine eye (dibba-cakkhu), he sees visible objects; with the divine ear-element (dibba-sota), he hears sounds. Visible base (rūpāyatana) is related to eye-consciousness (cakkhu-viññāṇa) by pre-existence condition. Sound base (saddāyatana) is related to ear-consciousness... smell base to nose-consciousness... taste base to tongue-consciousness... touch base to body-consciousness by pre-existence condition.

Ear base (sotāyatana) is related to ear-consciousness... nose base to nose-consciousness... tongue base to tongue-consciousness... body base to body-consciousness by pre-existence condition. Base-matter is related to resultant indeterminate and functional indeterminate aggregates by pre-existence condition. (1)
